free_tier.stated: /48 IPv6 (Free): Full /48 prefix, Instant deployment, RPKI ROA and route object, $0. The same page prices the larger blocks: /44 $20/yr, /40 $100/yr, /36 $200/yr, /29 $200/mo, and IPv6 Registration at $300 one-time (IPv6 prefix allocation, ARIN or RIPE PI with full control, a company is required).
free_tier.notes: The $0 is the checkout total of an orderable product: the /48 IPv6 (Free) checkout at my.ipye.com/products/ipv6-rental/48-ipv6/checkout lists Full /48 Prefix, Instant Deployment and Limited Support, and its order summary reads Total today: $0.00.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a prefix, not an object. The nearest equivalent is the block size, and the free allocation is one /48, which the page states as Free · 65,536 /64s
per_object_cap.notes: Anything larger is a paid tier: /44 is 16 × /48 at $20/yr, /40 is 256 × /48 at $100/yr, /36 is 4,096 × /48 at $200/yr, /29 is monthly at $200.

retention.stated: not applicable: a routed prefix, not stored bytes. No term is stated for the free /48; /44, /40 and /36 are labelled Yearly and the /29 Monthly
retention.notes: /ipv6-rental states no duration for the free /48, while the /44, /40 and /36 are yearly and the /29 monthly. Whether the free /48 persists indefinitely is unverified: no term for it is published.

egress.terms: No traffic term is published for a leased prefix: IPYE assigns the prefix to the lessee's compute hardware, which announces it, so the traffic crosses no IPYE port. The traffic statement on /use-cases belongs to the server bundles: 'Our Datacenter Bundles come natively provisioned with 10 Gbps unmetered upstream ports, ensuring your commercial VPNs never face peak-hour throttling, scaling transparently as active users surge.' ipye.com/servers lists the Datacenter Bundle on a 1 Gbps unmetered port, so the two pages give different ports for the Datacenter Bundle.
egress.free_allowance: none published; a prefix carries no traffic of its own

interface_detail: Ordering is a web checkout: my.ipye.com/products/ipv6-rental/48-ipv6/checkout requires ASN(s), Region and Intended Use, takes Name Servers for rDNS as optional, and shows an order summary of Total today: $0.00. No endpoint for ordering or for prefix management is documented; the vendor's API covers reverse DNS and geolocation. The prefix itself is reached by announcing it over BGP from the lessee's own routing daemon, a network interface with no token in the interface vocabulary.
tooling: A BGP routing daemon on the host that originates the prefix, and a Letter of Authorization from the portal ('Generate Letters of Authorization securely on demand.'). Ordering is a web form and the portal is the management surface, so no wrapper is needed. The one programmatic path is the rDNS and GeoIP API, behind an account: 'Take absolute control via our API and dashboard. Manage Reverse DNS zones, push bulk PTR record updates, and intuitively control WHOIS location configurations instantly.'
chaining: Announce the free /48 under an origin ASN from compute the user runs, and every request leaving that host presents an address inside one /48 of 65,536 /64s. That is one prefix behind one origin ASN: it meets a gate that counts the /64 and not a gate that counts the ASN.

limits.value: an origin ASN must exist before the prefix can be announced; the checkout refuses the order without ASN(s), Region and Intended Use
the free allocation is one /48 (65,536 /64s); a /44 is the next size and costs $20/yr
none published for a prefix; ipye.com/servers lists the Datacenter Bundle on a 1 Gbps unmetered port, while ipye.com/use-cases says 10 Gbps unmetered upstream ports for the Datacenter Bundles
no term stated for the free /48; /44, /40 and /36 are yearly and the /29 monthly, so a paid prefix is committed for a year

limits_note: Outside the limit vocabulary: ASN Registration at $500 one-time puts a permanent ASN under the buyer's company and needs 'a Company Registration Certificate (LLC, LTD), proof of ID for the administrative contact, and a signed framework agreement'; new RIR registrations typically take 2 to 7 business days. Shared ASN ($300/yr) and Dedicated ASN Rental ($700/yr) deploy instantly without those documents, and either one originates a prefix rented from IPYE ('If you rent IPs from us and a Dedicated or Shared ASN from us, everything connects natively.').
binding_note: write-gated binds first: the free /48 cannot be announced until an origin ASN exists ('Announcing the prefix needs an origin ASN. Use one you already operate, or add a shared or dedicated ASN from IPYE.'). The prefix carries no traffic allowance of its own, so no byte quota applies to it.

identity_cost.detail: An account at my.ipye.com is required to order, and the vendor says the account costs no identity document: the homepage carries 'No KYC/ID Verification Required', the /asn page description reads 'Crypto accepted, no KYC required', and the free /48 checkout asks for ASN(s), Region and Intended Use rather than a document. The exception is a different product on the same site: ASN Registration at $500 one-time requires a Company Registration Certificate (LLC, LTD), proof of ID for the administrative contact and a signed framework agreement. A rented shared ($300/yr) or dedicated ($700/yr) ASN is not described as requiring any of that.

reliability_note: One prefix is one network: every address in the free /48 is announced by the same origin ASN, so a gate counting the ASN or the prefix sees one source however many addresses are used. 'We don't shut down your servers for typical bulk operations' is a vendor statement with no measurement behind it. /use-cases says 'We lease prefixes registered to eyeball broadband networks and assign them to your compute hardware' of its ISP Network Subnets; whether the free /48 is registered that way is unverified.
confidence_note: Documented, not measured. RIPE stat searchcomplete for the string IPYE returns an empty category list, so no ASN registered under that name is findable in RIPE and the ASN behind the Shared ASN product cannot be named before an order. Measured would need an issued prefix, its registration checked in RIPE, and a refusal captured from an upstream that refuses Cloudflare's ranges.

notes: The free /48 is a prefix from IPYE at a fixed size and price: $0, 65,536 /64s, deployed immediately, with the same automatic RPKI ROA and route object as the paid sizes, and unannounced until an origin ASN carries it. /ipv6-rental makes no registration-class claim for it. Its FAQ answers 'Can I use these for proxies?' with yes and says the page is the prefix alone.
